name: Nationalpark Hohe Tauern
kurzbeschreibung: The Hohe Tauern National Park is the largest nature reserve in the Alps: Großglockner (3,798 m), pristine glaciers, golden eagles, and Matrei visitor centre.
beschreibung:
Overview

The Hohe Tauern National Park (Nationalpark Hohe Tauern) is the oldest and, covering more than 1,856 square kilometres, by far the largest protected nature reserve across the entire alpine arc and Central Europe. Established in 1981, this high-mountain national park spans the three Austrian federal provinces of Tyrol (East Tyrol), Salzburg, and Carinthia. Encompassing more than 300 peaks exceeding 3,000 metres in altitude – crowned by the Großglockner (3,798 m) and the Großvenediger (3,657 m) –, approximately 180 square kilometres of glacial expanses, and primeval mountain valleys, the park represents a globally renowned sanctuary of alpine biodiversity.

Wilderness, Biodiversity & National Park Centre

The landscapes within the national park range from montane larch and Swiss pine forests to subalpine meadows and high-alpine tundra and glaciated rockscapes. Thanks to stringent nature conservation protocols, more than 10,000 animal species and over 1,800 plant varieties flourish here. Symbolic species include alpine ibexes, chamois, marmots, and the kings of the sky: the majestic golden eagle and the successfully reintroduced bearded vulture. The cultural and interpretive centrepiece of the Tyrolean section is the Nationalparkhaus Matrei in Osttirol: its cutting-edge permanent exhibition "Tauernblicke – Moments of Wonder" takes visitors on a multimedia journey through the mysteries of the Hohe Tauern with 360-degree cinema, 3D interactive terrain models, and ranger stations. Spectacular natural landmarks in the Tyrolean sector include the thundering Umbalfälle waterfalls in the Virgental valley, the Innergschlöss glacier interpretive trail, and the scenic Kalser Glocknerstraße.

Visit & Arrival

The Hohe Tauern National Park and its extensive network of hiking trails are accessible 24 hours a day, 365 days a year, completely free of charge. The Nationalparkhaus in Matrei (Kirchplatz 2) is open during the summer season (June to September) daily from 09:00 to 17:00 (winter Mon–Fri 09:00–16:00; exhibition admission: Adults approx. €8.00, children free; completely free with the Osttirol Card). Daily guided tours are offered by certified National Park Rangers. Arrival by car: From the north via the Felbertauern road B108 directly to Matrei in Osttirol; from the south via Lienz (B108). By public transport: Rail (ÖBB) to Lienz station, connecting with VVT bus line 951/952 departing hourly for Matrei in Osttirol.

Tips

The Nationalparkhaus in Matrei and the viewing platforms along the Umbal Waterfalls trail are barrier-free and fully accessible for wheelchairs. Please observe the strict conservation regulations inside the park: leaving marked paths in the core wilderness zone, wild camping, and picking protected alpine plants are strictly prohibited. Book a ranger-led wildlife safari in the Kalser Ködnitztal valley.
